base.description: CRS510-8XS-2XQ-IN - eight 25G SFP28 cages, two 100G QSFP28 cages, a 100 Megabit management port with PoE in, an RJ45 console, a DC jack and a two-pin DC terminal, with two hot-swap AC supplies (part of the chassis in this model) and two fans. The box holds two power cords, rack ears and a fastening set.

description: MikroTik CRS510-8XS-2XQ-IN is a fixed 1U indoor Cloud Router Switch, 320 mm wide with rack ears in the box, with eight 25 Gigabit SFP28 cages and two 100 Gigabit QSFP28 cages, a 100 Megabit management port that also takes PoE in, an RJ45 serial console, a DC jack and a two-pin DC terminal (both placed as parts, see the gaps), and runs RouterOS v7. Everything is on the front: two hot-swap AC supply modules with their C14 inlets at the left, four stacks of two SFP28 cages, the QSFP28 stack, the console over the management port, RESET, the two DC inputs and three status lamps. Two fan openings and an earthing stud are on the rear. The brochure prints no part number for the supplies, so they are part of the chassis and there are no bays.

gaps.note: The brochure's text says the switch chip takes "only up to 27W (without attachments)" and its table prints 31 W maximum power consumption without attachments. The table's 31 W and its 51 W maximum are carried.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of the figure without attachments.

gaps.note: The brochure calls the two power supplies hot-swap and prints no part number; no data sheet or drawing of the supply is held, and no document says what the box ships with or what covers an empty slot. They are drawn as part of the chassis with their inlets and no bay is added; the base configuration exports two AC power ports.
gaps.wanted: The supply's part number and a statement of what a slot holds when empty.

gaps.note: The drawing and photograph 2232 show a DC barrel jack, 10.3 x 11.8 mm, rated 36-57 V (brochure and legend). It is the placed common/dc-barrel@1 (12 x 13 mm), which presents the dc-barrel interface the barrel plug mates, carrying the voltage and no current: no held document states a current or a barrel size for this jack. The part's own drawing of the socket stands in for the photographed one.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's current rating and barrel size for the DC jack.

gaps.note: The drawing and photograph 2232 show a two-pin pluggable DC terminal, 11.4 x 11.8 mm, beside the DC jack. It is the placed common/terminal-header-508-2@3 (12.16 x 8.6 mm), the two-position pluggable header the library already draws, which presents the terminal-508-2 interface a two-way plug mates. No held document states the terminal's pitch, so the 5.08 mm pitch of that part is an estimate: the drawing's 11.4 mm housing is about two positions of that pitch. The header is drawn empty and the photographed plug, with its wire entries, is not drawn above it. The brochure lists the terminal as a DC input (36-57 V).
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's statement of the terminal's pitch, or a drawing of the plug.

gaps.note: The photograph shows the USER, FAULT and POWER bars light grey and the supply lamp lit green. A lamp rests at its part's unlit colour, #3a3938, so the three bars read darker than the photograph and the supply lamps are unlit.

Photograph 2232 shows the SFP28 and QSFP28 cages as grey metal frames with a bright silver tab and a grey lamp strip. The shared cage parts draw near-black openings, and changing them would move boxes this one does not own, so the frames stay as the parts draw them.
gaps.wanted: A cage-frame skin for the shared SFP28 and QSFP28 parts, seated by this box.

gaps.note: The earth symbol on the rear is black in photograph 2233; the shared symbol part draws it pale and has no colour field.
gaps.wanted: A symbol colour on the shared part, or a version seated by this box.

gaps.note: Searched the brochure, the page and the quick guide page for an LED table: none. The arrow lamps, the QSFP28's two round lamps, the USER, FAULT and POWER lamps and the green lamp on each supply carry the component's own vocabulary and no meaning is stated.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's LED description for the CRS510-8XS-2XQ-IN.

gaps.note: No held document shows the left wall: the drawing has no wall view and the photographs show the right wall, the front and the rear. It is left empty and is not drawn from the right.
The top plan shows four shallow slots in the lid and the CLOUD SWITCH lettering, which photograph 2232 shows as embossed grooves and not as openings; no document shows the underside.
The brochure and the page give no fan count and no fan statement; the rear photograph shows two openings, which are drawn. No fan redundancy is written.
gaps.wanted: MikroTik's fan count and redundancy statement.

gaps.note: Neither the brochure nor the page gives a weight.
The saved product page carries no Discontinued badge and MikroTik publishes no end-of-life page, so no lifecycle is written.

name: crs510-8xs-2xq-in

built-in-power-and-fans.note: The brochure lists two AC inputs and "dual hot-swap power supplies". The drawing and photograph 2232 show two modules at the front, each with a C14 inlet, a steel handle, a latch and a green lamp. No held document prints a part number for the supply (the brochure, the page, the quick guide page and the drawing were searched), so none is named: the supplies are part of the chassis with their inlets, as on juniper/ex2300-24t, and there are no bays (gap `hot-swap-supplies`). No document says what covers an empty slot. The photograph prints "100-240 V 50/60 Hz" up the left edge of the first module and PSU 1 and PSU 2 beside them. The brochure's 51 W is the box's maximum power consumption. The rear photograph shows two fan openings, each a ring of mesh round a plain hub about 19 mm across (read at 5.3 px per mm); the brochure and the page give no fan count and no fan statement.

chassis.note: 320 wide, 44 high, 185 deep, as the drawing prints them; the brochure prints 320 x 185 x 44 and agrees. The drawing also dimensions 9 mm beyond the front (the two-pin terminal block), 8 mm beyond the rear (the earthing stud) and 210 mm overall to the ends of the supply handles; none of these is part of the 185. The 481 mm across the ears is the ears' width, and the 462 mm the pitch of their holes.

colour.note: Each value is the median of a plain area, away from ports, lamps, labels and text, taken with a script over the photograph's pixels. The face is #d2d0d0: photograph 2232, box 1500,750 to 2400,785 (31500 pixels), the plain strip of the front face above the cages, and it is drawn so. The earlier #e7e6e9 (box 1500,520 to 1700,560) is the lid, which the photograph lights from above, and #dddddd was the library's light-stage value; the rear reads #c1bfbe (2233, box 2000,800 to 2800,850, 40000 pixels) and #bebcbc beside it, so the single chassis colour is the front's. The supply modules are #a3a5a7, the channel-wise median of three plain patches of 2232, which lights the plate from above: box 377,1031 to 562,1042 #a3a5a7 (2035 pixels), box 448,856 to 496,878 #abafb1 (1056 pixels, spread 22) and box 440,1016 to 500,1040 #a2a5a7 (1440 pixels, spread 59); no clean patch of the plate reads lighter (the brighter pixels in the photograph are the handle and the module's lit edge). The group bars are the photograph's purple: bar-25g #938ac6 (2232, box 1505,810 to 1513,855, 360 pixels, spread 26; box 1505,965 to 1513,1005 gives #9289c6) and bar-100g #8e85c3 (box 2160,960 to 2175,1012, 780 pixels, spread 12). Their lettering is light, as the photograph prints it: #d5d4d7 on the 25G bar (the pixels above 205 in box 1505,865 to 1522,955, 149 pixels, spread 15) and #d2d1d4 on the 100G bar (box 2160,845 to 2175,950, 318 pixels, spread 11). The jack plate is #949290: 2232, box 2558,845 to 2572,930 (1190 pixels; box 2428,830 to 2438,910, 800 pixels, gives #93918f). The unlit lamps read #878686, #858584 and #898888 (2232, the lamps note gives the boxes). The rear's face reads #bebcbc in 2233 (box 2180,870 to 2910,1020, 109500 pixels).

datasheet.note: The brochure is MikroTik's datasheet for the model: product code CRS510-8XS-2XQ-IN, QCA9531 650 MHz MIPSBE, 128 MB RAM, 32 MB flash, 1 x 100M Ethernet, 8 x 25G SFP28, 2 x 100G QSFP28, switch chip 98DX4310, 320 x 185 x 44 mm, RouterOS v7 level 5, -40 to +70 C. Powering: three DC inputs (PoE-in 43-57 V passive or 802.3bt class 6; DC jack 36-57 V; 2-pin terminal 36-57 V), two AC inputs at 100-240 V and 47-63 Hz, 31 W without attachments and 51 W at most. Included parts: 2 power cords, a fastening set, rack ears. The text says "dual hot-swap power supplies" and states no redundancy form. Each figure is filed as the document words it.

dc-inputs.note: Both DC inputs are placed parts: the jack as common/dc-barrel@1 and the terminal as common/terminal-header-508-2@3 (gaps `dc-jack` and `dc-terminal`), each centred on the housing the drawing and photograph 2232 show; the photograph prints "36-57 V" over both DC inputs. The two-pin pluggable terminal block is 11.4 x 11.8 mm at 275.4 mm, 24.8 mm down, read off the drawing's front view at 3.9375 px per mm (outer extent 317 x 330 px at 7 times enlargement, less the line weight): a cap 10.4 x 3.9 over a body 11.4 x 7.9 and two wire entries 3.6 x 5.1 mm on a 5.05 mm pitch. The drawing dimensions it 9 mm proud of the front; the header is drawn empty and the cap and entries of the photographed plug are not drawn above it. The registry's common/dc-terminal-plug-2 is a 32.1 x 17.6 mm part drawn for another maker's box, so the two-position header is placed instead. The legends are as the photograph prints them: one bracket over both inputs, "36-57 V" centred over it (the earlier drawing put it over the jack alone), a circled minus then a circled plus over the terminal, and over the jack a circled minus, the barrel symbol with its centre pin dot joined to the circled plus: the centre pin is the positive pole. The legend positions are read off photograph 2232 at 34.96 px per mm across and 30.7 px per mm down (the jack housing is 358 px for 11.8 mm), anchored on the jack's and the terminal's lower edge, to about 0.4 mm across and 0.8 mm down. The jack is 10.3 x 11.8 mm at 290.1 mm, 24.8 mm down; the part's own drawing of the socket stands in for the photographed one.

ears.note: Rack ears are in the box (the brochure and the page: Rack ears). The drawing's front view draws them 80.5 mm either side of the 320 mm body (481 mm over the ears, holes 462 mm apart). They are shipped flush with the face and are not drawn on it; no `at` is written and no kit is listed.

finish-and-fittings.note: Every value is the median of a named region of photographs 2232 (front) and 2233 (rear), estimated. The console and management jacks are set to the plate's #949290 with the jack part's `finish` field. Each supply has a steel handle, #a4a4a1 (2232, box 512,825 to 544,1012, 5984 pixels) with a lit edge #e2e2e2 read by eye, that runs the full height of the face and past the module; a blue-grey release latch at its left, #4b4d5b (2232, box 375,850 to 395,920, 1400 pixels); and printed ring marks beside the module, three columns of two, whose #bdbbbb is by eye against the face. Positions are read from the photographs to about 2 mm. The 25G and 100G bar lettering is drawn at 2.4 mm and the supply legends at 2.0 mm, from the letters' extent in 2232 (about 1.7 mm per character on the bars). Each fan carries two corner screws, #c4c3c2 (2233, box 1405,816 to 1423,834, 324 pixels), and the two fan rings are centred 2.5 mm right of the first reading (2233: 119.7 and 160.0 mm). The earth stud is placed as the MikroTik stud part, as on the CRS309, in place of two discs of art.

front-layout.note: From the drawing's front view. Two supply modules 52.1 x 38.5 mm at 12.6 and 72.0 mm, 2.1 mm down, each with a C14 inlet turned a quarter turn (17.7 wide by 25.5 tall, earth pin at the left) centred 49.45 and 108.85 mm and 23.5 mm down, a green lamp, a six-slot vent and a latch. Four stacks of two SFP28 cages, stack centres 153.6, 171.0, 192.1 and 209.5 mm (a 17.4 mm pitch inside a pair and 21.1 mm between pairs), the openings centred 15.7 and 30.9 mm, and a middle strip 23.0 mm down with four arrow lamps read at -4.6, -1.9, +1.9 and +4.7 mm from the centre (a down, up, down and up arrow). One QSFP28 stack centred at 233.3 mm, drawn 21.0 mm wide, with a strip carrying a down and an up arrow, two round lamps and a down and an up arrow again, read at -7.5, -5.1, -2.0, +1.9, +5.0 and +7.3 mm. The console and management jacks share a plate 17.6 x 26.6 at 248.2 mm, 10.0 mm, the console above. RESET is a ring at 270.7 mm, 31.9 mm. The two-pin terminal block is 11.4 x 11.8 at 275.4 mm and the DC jack housing 10.3 x 11.8 at 290.1 mm, both 24.8 mm down. Three lamps are small bars under the jacks at 267.1, 274.0 and 288.2 mm, 38.6 mm.

gate-1.note: The drawing's front view body is 3780 px wide at 3 times enlargement for the printed 320 (3.9375 px per mm in the page image) and 513 px tall between the lip lines, which reads 43.4 mm, the printed 44. Every x and y below is taken at 3.9375 px per mm from the body's top-left corner of the front view, to about 0.4 mm.

lamps.note: The four arrow lamps of a stack: an arrow points at the cage it belongs to, so a down arrow is the lower cage and an up arrow the upper one. They are carried symmetric about the stack centre (at -4.65, -2.05, +2.05 and +4.65 mm for the SFP28, 0.1 to 0.4 mm from the reading) and the QSFP28's at -7.4, -5.1, +5.1 and +7.4 mm with its two round lamps at -2.1 and +2.1 mm. Which pair of a stack is the speed lamp and which the activity lamp is not stated by a document, and the QSFP28's two round lamps name no cage that a document states (gap `led-states`); they are drawn for the chassis. The three bar lamps are printed USER, FAULT and POWER (photograph 2232), and show unlit grey there (#878686, #858584 and #898888: medians of 225, 225 and 207 pixels, boxes 2565,1028 to 2590,1037, 2625,1028 to 2650,1037 and 2750,1028 to 2773,1037). The render draws them in the resting colour of common/led-rect@2, #3a3938, a dark grey: the component's own median of 27 unlit lamps in two MikroTik photographs, which disagree (this photograph's three bars read lighter than that), and no placement sets it. Their place and size agree with the drawing. The green lamp on each supply module is lit in the photograph (#5e6d52, median of 193 pixels within 8 px of 484,831) and drawn here in the resting colour of common/led-dot@1, which is a dark grey, also left as the component draws it.

management-and-console.note: Photograph 2232 prints CONSOLE over the upper jack and MGMT/PoE in under the lower. The page counts one 100M Ethernet port, the management port, filed at 100m; the brochure lists PoE in at 43-57 V passive or 802.3bt class 6 on it, which is an input and is carried in the power attributes, not as a PoE out.

port-numbering.note: The metal prints 2 4 6 8 over the SFP28 stacks and 1 3 5 7 under them, and 2 over and 1 under the QSFP28 stack, so the lower cage of a stack takes the odd number. The groups are printed 25G SFP28 and 100G QSFP28 on a purple bar at the left of each group.

rear-layout.note: From photograph 2233 (the rear, from above), x across the 320 mm at 5.3 px per mm and y estimated (the photograph looks down). Two fan openings 36 mm across, centred 117.0 and 158.5 mm and 23.0 mm down; an earthing stud at 12.3 mm and 33.7 mm with its earth mark above it. Read to about 2 mm, as seen from behind. The hexagon field is measured on 2233 at 8.84 px per mm (the face is 2830 px across the printed 320 mm), estimated: on a fan guard (box 1125,805 to 1465,1080; 21 whole openings) an opening is 5.32 mm across its corners and 4.07 mm across its flats, the column step 4.71 mm and the same-column pitch 5.31 mm. It was the renderer's plain vent tile (8.86 x 5.11 mm, hexagons 5.1 mm across the corners on a 4.43 mm column step), which `pattern-pitch` cannot give the metal's webs, so each field is a `motif` tile of one regular hexagon period, 9.41 x 5.43 mm with openings 5.32 mm across the corners (the nearest-neighbour distance is 5.43 mm), whose lattice starts on a hexagon centred under each hub, as the photograph shows. The `pattern-pitch` of each is its tile.

side-layout.note: Photograph 2234 shows a field of hexagonal perforations on the right wall, behind the front. It is drawn 55 x 26 mm, 33 mm from the front and 9 mm down, read off the photograph, which looks at the wall obliquely (about 8 mm). No held document shows the left wall. The drawing's end view shows the front's mounting screws and the supply handles, not a wall.

vent-slots.note: Each supply's vent is slots, as the drawing's front view and photograph 2232 show, not round perforations: six tall slots (three across, two down) under the handle and a row of four short ones along the top edge, the first of them left of the handle and three right of it. Read at the drawing page's 3.94 px per mm (the 320 mm body is 1261 px) to about 0.4 mm: a tall slot 3.8 mm wide and 7.6 mm high (7.5 for the lower row) on a 5.0 mm pitch across and a 9.2 mm pitch down, the first 3.7 mm in from the module's left edge and 20.0 mm and 29.2 mm down; a short slot 2.5 mm high, 5.2 mm down, 6.1 to 6.3 mm wide, at 11.0, 27.1, 34.6 and 41.9 mm from the module's left edge. The second supply is the first at a 59.4 mm offset. Photograph 2232, at 8.74 px per mm, shows the same grid (slots 3.4 by 6.7 mm on a 5.0 and 8.4 mm pitch, the photograph looking slightly down on the face) and the same four short slots. The photograph hints at a fourth tall column behind the handle (a sliver shows at its right edge); the drawing shows nothing there, so none is drawn.
